newsitem.title: GREECE: KARATZAS CALLS FOR TAX REFORMS, ABOLITION OF EFTE TAX.
newsitem.headline: KARATZAS CALLS FOR TAX REFORMS, ABOLITION OF EFTE TAX.

text.p: Hellenic Bank Association president Theodore Karatzas called on the government to reform the country's tax system on securities, primary and secondary capital markets, abolish the EFTE tax and modernise the bankruptcy code.
Karatzas, president of the state National Bank of Greece was speaking before the general assembly of the Hellenic Bank Association which celebrated its 70th anniversary.
Greek banks have long complained about the distortionary effects of the special tax on banking services (EFTE) that partially explains the lending-deposit drachma interest rate spread.

The long awaited national payments system should be finally developed, the private and public sectors should produce higher quality statistical data and bank asset valuation principles should be improved, he said.

The imposition of high reserve requirements on bank deposits was hurting Greek banks, making them less effective in a highly competitive banking environment that was becoming more integrated, Karatzas added. --Dimitris Kontogiannis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4 (c) Reuters Limited 1997
